Break near-ties on grant purpose and filing presence

Source: R/purpose.R
pf_purpose_tiebreak.Rd

Recomputes the overall pick for grants where the top candidates are within tie_band of each other, ordering the contenders by the configured keys instead of by score. Scores are not modified, so the YES / MAYBE / NO thresholds keep their meaning and the benchmark stays comparable; only the choice among tied candidates changes.

Usage

pf_purpose_tiebreak(x, org_text, config = pf_tiebreak_config())

Arguments

x

A pf_match from pf_match_grants().

org_text

Output of pf_build_org_text().

config

Output of pf_tiebreak_config().

Value

x with result$overall_* rewritten where the tiebreak fired, plus tiebreak_fired, tiebreak_key, and tiebreak_from_ein columns recording every change.

Details

Features are computed lazily, for contending candidates only — a few thousand pairs rather than the millions the cascade scored.

What the keys are worth

On the 61 contested adjudicated grants, ordering by cov_all then has_mission inside the band gains 3 and loses 0 (0.770 -> 0.820) with tie_high = 0, or gains 1 and loses 0 at tie_high = 0.95. On the 794 YES grants it changes nothing, because none of them are inside the band. Note that npmatch's own tiebreak = "name" key is net 0 to −2 on this data: it assumes the entity whose full name matches the query is the right one, and in 990-PF grants the correct recipient is the FOUNDATION arm 52.8% of the time, so the assumption is a coin flip here.
